issues.description: Tab is no longer accepted to confirm completion when the option is off, breaking the documented fallback
issues.detail: The tooltip promises 'completions will be accepted with the Tab key only.' The code says `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` -- so Tab skips the early return, but then falls through into the giant elif chain below that handles Enter/Return/Tab acceptance. Re-read it: when the option is off and the user hits Tab, this code path does the right thing only by accident of the surrounding logic. Verify by actually pressing Tab. If it doesn't accept, the patch is a lie. Add a test.

issues.description: New branch intercepts every non-Tab key including arrows, Escape, Backspace, Ctrl+anything
issues.detail: The condition is `not key == Qt.Key_Tab`. That means when the option is disabled, ANY key that isn't Tab -- arrow keys, PageUp/PageDown to navigate the list, Escape to dismiss, Ctrl+C -- gets the popup hidden and the event forwarded to the textedit. The popup becomes unusable. The check needs to be `key in (Qt.Key_Return, Qt.Key_Enter)`, not 'everything that isn't Tab.' This is the bug.

issues.description: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is bad style; write `key != Qt.Key_Tab`
issues.detail: Python operator precedence makes this parse correctly but every reader has to stop and check. `key != Qt.Key_Tab` is what you mean. This is the kind of micro-cleverness that wastes the next maintainer's attention budget. Two characters shorter and unambiguous.

issues.description: Zero test coverage for a keybinding behavior change
issues.detail: This patch changes how Enter and Tab interact with the completion popup -- the single most-pressed key combination in the editor. There is no test in the diff that exercises option=True/Enter, option=False/Enter, option=False/Tab, option=False/Arrow. Prose in the PR description is not a regression suite. Add the four cases.

issues.description: Grid row 4 inserted but row 5 (hint-after-idle) left unchanged, leaving an empty row 4-to-5 gap implicitly
issues.detail: The shift moved completions_after_characters from row 3 to row 4. completions_hint_after_idle stays at row 5. Visually fine in Qt's grid since empty rows collapse, but worth double-checking the rendered confpage actually looks right and no row was supposed to move with it.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The intent is fine and the config plumbing is correct, but the keyPressEvent change is wrong-shape: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` means every non-Tab key (arrows, Escape, PageUp/Down, Ctrl-modifiers) hides the popup and forwards the event, which breaks navigation and dismissal of the completion list. The check should be an explicit allowlist of Enter/Return, not a denylist around Tab. Also: no tests for a keybinding change that touches the hottest key path in the editor, and `not key == X` should be `key != X`. Fix the predicate, add four small tests (option on/off x Enter/Tab/Arrow), resubmit.
